items.followUp: A moving ball collides with a stationary ball. Explain what happens to the total momentum of the two-ball system if no external force acts.

rubric.why: Checks the statement of the law and its condition, or the equivalent momentum equation.
rubric.description: States that total momentum remains constant when no external force acts on the system.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the conservation statement with the no-external-force condition, or an equivalent momentum equation.

rubric.why: Checks that the example involves a moving ball colliding with a stationary ball.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the moving and stationary balls.

rubric.why: Checks that the example demonstrates conservation of the balls' combined momentum.
rubric.description: Explains that momentum is transferred between the balls while their combined momentum remains unchanged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for explaining both the transfer and the unchanged combined momentum.

modelAnswer: The law of conservation of momentum states that the total momentum of a system remains constant if no external force acts on it.
For example, when a moving ball collides with a stationary ball, momentum is transferred between the balls.
The combined momentum of the two balls remains unchanged: their total momentum before collision equals their total momentum after collision.

items.followUp: A 2 kg object is thrown vertically upwards at 10 m s⁻¹. Find its maximum gravitational potential energy and its kinetic energy when it returns to the starting point, neglecting air resistance.

rubric.why: Checks that the mass is converted to SI units and the initial velocity is identified.
rubric.description: Writes the mass and initial velocity in SI units.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for m = 0.5 kg and u = 15 m s⁻¹.

rubric.why: Checks the energy relation used to find the potential energy at maximum height.
rubric.description: Uses the conversion of the initial kinetic energy into maximum potential energy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that maximum P.E. equals initial K.E. or giving the equivalent energy formula.

rubric.why: Checks the calculated maximum potential energy.
rubric.description: Finds the maximum P.E. as 56.25 J.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct maximum P.E. with unit.

rubric.why: Checks that the stone's kinetic energy on reaching the ground is correctly found and reported.
rubric.description: Finds the K.E. when the stone hits the ground.
rubric.how: Award 2 marks for the correct relation or working and the answer 56.25 J.

modelAnswer: Given: m = 500 g = 0.5 kg; initial velocity u = 15 m s⁻¹.
At maximum height, P.E. = initial K.E. = ½mu².
Neglecting air resistance, the K.E. when the stone hits the ground equals its initial K.E.
